resumo: A costume improvised at home makes as many photos as a packed street parade, and nobody comes home exhausted.

secoes.titulo: Carnival with a small child happens at home
secoes.texto: A street parade means crowds, loud music and strong sun, and none of that suits someone a few months old. The costume, the music and the mayhem work perfectly in the living room, and produce the same photos with none of the problems.

itens: Children's ear defenders. Parade sound is far too loud for small ears.
Guaranteed shade and a time outside the peak sun.
Stay at the edge, never in the middle, and know your way out.
A children's street parade, in the morning, is another matter entirely: smaller, shorter and made for this.
Agree beforehand with whoever is with you how long you are staying, and stick to it.

secoes.texto: Comfortable beats pretty. Light fabric, no tight elastic, no hood that makes her hot, nothing glued on that could end up in her mouth. A costume improvised from what you have at home usually makes a better photo than a bought one.

itens: The photo of the whole costume, full length, in the best light there is.
The face, close up, with the paint or the accessory.
A short video dancing with her in your arms.
The sleepy face at the end, which is always the best photo of the day.
Two written lines: what the costume was, who chose it and why.
